COMMENT_COUNT SCHEMA SPLIT CONFIRMED BOTH WAYS. New install: comment_count is ABSENT from wp_mvs_media_index, while view_count and reaction_count are both still present, so only the intended column went. Upgraded install (this dev site, mvs_db_version 36): the column is still PRESENT, as intended for existing sites. TWO FALSE ALARMS I CHASED DOWN THIS ROUND, recorded so the next walker does not repeat them. (1) The Load More focus ring measured 0px once - an artefact of calling focus() in the same tick as the Load More re-render. Re-measured with a settle delay it is 2px in all four states; the CSS rule is present in the stylesheet. (2) At 390px a hit-test reported the bulk bar's Delete, Select all and Clear as 'blocked' by .mvs-confirm-overlay. The overlay is a hidden template - display:none, hidden attribute, 0x0 rect, offsetParent null - and the three controls simply sat below the fold at that viewport, where elementFromPoint returns null. The decisive check: Playwright really clicked Delete and the confirm dialog opened. Nothing is intercepting.

ALBUM PICKER SCOPING CONFIRMED, AND IT IS NOT A PRIVACY FIX. With author=<viewer> the REST response carries only the viewer's own albums and no other member's titles: mina_aoki gets exactly [Tokyo Streets, author 8], admin gets exactly [Field Notes, author 1]. Worth being precise about what changed: the scoping is client-side - the picker now sends the parameter - and an unscoped GET /mvs/v1/albums still returns every album a viewer is allowed to see, which for this fixture is nine public albums including other members' titles. That is not a leak, and I probed it: flipping album 238 to private removed it from BOTH another member's and an anonymous visitor's unscoped listing (8 items, 238 absent), so the endpoint is privacy-gated server-side and the picker change is a UX scoping improvement on top of it. Album 238 restored to public.

PRECONDITION TO ADD TO THE RUNBOOK - assert src vs build parity before a walk. Pro blocks register from MVS_PRO_DIR . 'build/blocks/' (includes/Blocks/BlockRegistrar.php:73-80), and build/ is gitignored (wpmediaverse-pro/.gitignore:23). It is refreshed only by an explicit build, so a clean git tree says nothing about what the site actually renders and the walked site can silently lag the source. That is exactly what happened with pro-document-embed: the fix was correct in src/ but build/ still held the pre-fix file, so the row read as a broken fix for a whole round trip. Packaging does run grunt build -> npm run build:blocks, so the zip would have shipped correct code - the risk is QA certifying a build the release does not contain, in either direction. Suggested check at the top of Global preconditions: for each src/blocks/*/render.php compare against build/blocks/<slug>/render.php and STOP if any differ, the same way a failing fixture cleanup is treated as a release blocker.

RUNBOOK MAINTENANCE DEBT - the runbook's own rule is that every customer-visible fix ships with a matching D row in the same PR. Eight fixes verified across these runs still have no D row: the grid query-budget batching, the Explore bulk-delete confirm-overlay context, the tag-autocomplete await, the pro-document-embed editor notice, the activation guard in delete_rows_without_media, the set() write-after-delete guard, the sticky-top offsets, and the album-picker author scoping. Highest value first: the set() guard wants a D row asserting that a write for a deleted id creates no row and logs nothing; the pro-document-embed case wants one asserting the notice renders from the BUILT file; the activation guard wants one running a migration whose cascade list names a table a later migration creates; the sticky offsets want one asserting each pinned surface clears the theme header at 1440 and 390.

RE-BASELINE THE QUERY ROW - C.member.grid-render-query-budget / D.grid-render-n-plus-1 still read 'under 6 DB queries per page', which no longer describes what is being protected. After the fix the cost is a fixed per-page floor that does not grow with tile count: mvs/media-grid measured in its own cold process at perPage 1 = 12 queries, perPage 12 = 13, perPage 24 = 15, so the marginal cost is about 0.13 queries per tile (was about 2.45) and 11 extra tiles cost 1 query (was 27). Real /media/ page: 105 total queries for 12 tiles (was 117), delta against a 1-tile tag page 14 (was 25). Rewrite the row as a per-page floor (about 12-13 on this fixture) plus a marginal per-tile ceiling. Render output has been stable at md5 864d7d596be16588198ee1cfb37aff92 across three stamps.

RUNBOOK CORRECTIONS the next editor should apply (verified against 2.5.1 code, not defects): (1) C.anon.single-media claims /p/<media_id>/ is the canonical MVS URL - it is not. /p/([0-9]+) is BuddyNext's route (buddynext/includes/Core/PageRouter.php:2358), so /p/<mvs media id>/ correctly 404s. MVS's own route is /media/<slug>/ -> mvs_media_slug, which BuddyNext redirects via the documented mvs_single_media_redirect filter; neutralising it for one request gives a 200 native page with h1, og:image, og:title, twitter:card, a 200 image/webp asset and 6 reaction buttons. (2) E.group-dm cites /mvs-pro/v1/groups/{id}/messages - that route does not exist; group creation is /mvs-pro/v1/groups and messaging goes through Free's /mvs/v1/conversations/{id}/messages. A non-member gets 404, not 403. (3) The Fixture cleanup block deletes mvs_reports WHERE reason LIKE 'smoke-%', but reason is an enum so that clause can never match - the marker belongs in details. (4) C.member.video-poster-fallback names PosterService::is_ffmpeg_available(), which does not exist; PosterService has only dir(), stage_bytes() and stage_client_frame(). (5) D.documents-privacy-vocabulary asserts PRIVACY_VALUES is exactly private/members/public - it is now private/space/members/public. The guarded bug is gone: nothing offers 'unlisted', and unlisted or restricted both answer 400 mvs_document_privacy_invalid. (6) C.member.lightbox-edit-modal says the Edit cog appears ONLY on /my-media/ cards - an owner also sees it in the Explore lightbox for their own media, which is not a leak (non-owner gets display:none, and PUT and DELETE answer 403). (7) C.member.bulk-trash-restore-delete describes Move to Trash plus a Trashed filter on /my-media/ - the member bulk bar offers Set privacy, Add to album, Add tags and Delete; trash lives on admin All Media. (8) A3/A4 should state that the competition routes and the /compete/ page depend on competitions being enabled, which is NOT the default (mvs_competitions_enabled ships '0'), otherwise a correct fresh install reads as four 404s and a missing page.
